chapter_title: Designing an A/B Test with Students
learning_objective: The learner will calculate the raw gain and the normalized gain for six students from their pre-test and post-test scores, with at least 5 of 6 cases fully correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** learning-gain-calculator
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the raw gain and the normalized gain for six students from their pre-test and post-test scores, with at least 5 of 6 cases fully correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Pre-Test, Post-Test, Learning Gain (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each case the learner enters the raw gain and the normalized gain. A case is fully correct when both match the Content table. Normalized gain is rounded to two decimal places, and the learner enters Undefined when the pre-test is 100. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 cases fully correct on the first attempt. Reading the formulas is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A larger raw gain always means more learning. (2) A negative gain cannot happen. (3) The normalized gain is always defined. **Instructional Rationale:** Calculating a gain from two scores is an Apply-level action. Cases with different starting points, a loss, and a perfect pre-test show why the normalized gain exists and where it fails. **Content:** The formulas, shown at all times: raw gain = post - pre. Normalized gain = (post - pre) / (100 - pre). The normalized gain is undefined when pre = 100. The six cases (all made up, scores out of 100): | # | Pre-test | Post-test | Raw gain | Normalized gain | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 40 | 70 | 30 | 0.50 | 30 divided by 60 is 0.50. | | 2 | 60 | 80 | 20 | 0.50 | 20 divided by 40 is 0.50. | | 3 | 20 | 50 | 30 | 0.38 | 30 divided by 80 is 0.375, which rounds to 0.38. | | 4 | 90 | 95 | 5 | 0.50 | 5 divided by 10 is 0.50, the same share of the room as case 1. | | 5 | 80 | 70 | -10 | -0.50 | The score fell, so both gains are negative. | | 6 | 100 | 100 | 0 | Undefined | There was no room to gain. | **Provenance:** The scores are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The normalized gain follows the chapter section "Learning Gain". **Rules:** Raw gain is an integer and may be negative. Normalized gain is rounded to two decimal places with 0.375 rounded to 0.38. A case is fully correct only when both entries match. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one pre-test and post-test pair and the formulas. 2. The learner enters the raw gain and the normalized gain, and presses Check. 3. The sim shows which entries were correct and the Why text. 4. After case 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 cases in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: raw gain [raw], normalized gain [normalized]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The raw gain is [raw] and the normalized gain is [normalized]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can calculate a learning gain." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed case. **Starting State:** The first case in the shuffled order, the formulas, and empty fields. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked examples are cases 1 and 4, which both give a normalized gain of 0.50.
